$comment: Credential-shaped parameters hidden in the URL FRAGMENT, where searchParams cannot see them.
intent: Documentation of intent, NOT a byte-enforcement contract. The decline predicate is a boolean gate on an unmodified URL: a URL that passes is byte-identical no matter which leg's parser matched, so legs cannot disagree about bytes — only about which of them declines. The effective guard is the UNION of every leg's predicate, and stricter is safe. A leg that fails to decline one of these shapes is not broken; it is contributing less than the others, and that is a gap worth closing rather than a test worth arguing with. NORMALIZATION is the opposite case and must stay identical across legs — see HINT-6.
query_vs_fragment_asymmetry: A valueless `?email` DECLINES while `#contact-email` CARRIES, and that difference is correct rather than an inconsistency to tidy away. The `?` has already established parameter space, so a bare name inside it is a flag-style parameter and `email` is credential-shaped. A fragment with no `?` carries no parameter-space signal at all; reading it as a parameter list would be an assumption, not a parse. Both unification directions are wrong: unifying toward the query side reintroduces the `#contact-email` false positive, and unifying toward the fragment side stops declining a genuine credential-shaped parameter.

cases.why: Hash-router route carrying a real OAuth callback in its query tail. Invisible to searchParams; the fragment is preserved by normalization, so without this check the grant leaves the browser verbatim.

OAuth implicit flow. No '?' anywhere, so a parser that only reads a '?' tail misses it silently. This is the shape where reasonable implementations most plausibly differ, which is why it is written down.
Control. A route, not a pair list — no '=' anywhere, so nothing is read as a parameter name.
Control. An in-page anchor, dropped by normalization as before. Must not be read as a parameter name.
Control. A fragment query tail carrying an ordinary view selector — the shape the decline rule must NOT over-catch, or every hash-router app with a filtered list becomes undiscoverable.

The pair to `anchor-named-like-a-credential` below, and the reason the two must not be unified. The `?` established parameter space, so a bare name is a flag-style parameter — see query_vs_fragment_asymmetry.
Control. Contains 'email', but has no '=' and therefore no value to leak. Matching it would decline an ordinary page to protect nothing.
